note: Portable byte representation of the frozen SP-14-v1 requirements for card SP1401-FLOW-GAPS, transcribed verbatim from the planner item. The acceptance launcher pins the SHA-256 of this file and records it in every receipt; any byte change yields a different evidence identity and is refused. Not a test input.

item.goal: Stop illustrative current streamlines at screen-resolved land gaps between integration probes.
item.premise: On a 128 by 64 synthetic eastward field, the unchanged integrator returns one line segment crossing a one-pixel null strip at x=24.5 to 25.5. A wider-strip control has no crossing. This is a pure sampler contract, not navigation or real terrain qualification.
item.scope: Add bounded segment-support sampling within flowPaths, at no more than one screen-pixel spacing including endpoints, before accepting each proposed five-pixel segment. Do not change integration direction, seed grid, caps, STEP_PX, MAX_STEPS, field interpolation, masks or drawing policy. This is a one-pixel screen-resolution guarantee, never an arbitrary subpixel geometry proof.
item.A1: With the synthetic one-pixel vertical gap used by the diagnostic, no emitted segment crosses the null strip; test complete segments, not just vertices. Mirror east/west and north/south and use diagonal segments through the center of a one-pixel blocked cell.
item.A2: A fully supported constant vector preserves baseline points, seed cap, fast flag, speed, direction and still-water behavior. Existing broad-gap, ragged-grid and boundary controls remain green.
item.A3: Count sampler calls and prove a constant bounded number per five-pixel segment, with sampling intervals at most one pixel. Zero-support, short path and viewport-edge inputs preserve existing results. Do not mutate the vector function, field or masks.
item.healthy: The identical eastward fixture with no blocked strip preserves the original supported line and direction.
item.fixture: Synthetic screen sampler and blocked-pixel masks shaped like tests/test_flow.mjs; no map service, raster or geographic source.
